route: No independent-means route found. Migri's 'other grounds' page says 'Usually, we can grant you a residence permit only if you have enough money for living in Finland' and its examples are a dating relationship with a Finn or an intended marriage, victims of trafficking. Migri FAQ: 'If you apply for a residence permit on some other grounds while in Finland, the decision will usually be negative.' Migri's insurance page is for students: 'must take out private insurance that will cover your medical and drug expenses' (EUR 120,000 for studies under two years; excess not above EUR 300).
policy: Kela: 'If you live in Finland permanently, you are covered under the Finnish national health insurance scheme.' Permanence is decided case by case; residents with a municipality of residence can use public healthcare. No premium was retrieved; Finnish health insurance contributions are collected through tax (rates not retrieved).
working: Not computed: no source for client fees or contributions, no private tariff.

uncertainty: No Finnish figures reached: the search tool hit its limit, Migri pages block curl (Cloudflare), and guessed Kela, Vero and THL URLs returned 404. Migri quotes came from the live page through the fetch tool, not saved.

statutory_must_pay.what: Covered by Kela's national health insurance once resident; the sairaanhoitomaksu is income-based (tax code). No fixed premium.

private_plan.product: Terveysvakuutus (health insurance), EUR 30,000 sum insured, EUR 150 deductible
private_plan.terms: Covers doctor fees, imaging, laboratory tests and surgery in Finland up to 30,000 EUR a year. Excludes medicines, preventive care, mental health and rehabilitation. It is a basic product; a comprehensive adult medical-expense policy is quoted at about 1,000 EUR a year (about 83 a month) in a Finnish money magazine, so the true mid-range figure may be higher.
private_plan.pricing: Nordea's price example for a 45-year-old: base price 33.72 EUR a month (28.58 for loan customers); x2 = 67.44.
